items.title: Matt Pavelich, first linesman in Hockey Hall of Fame, dead at 92
items.body: NEW YORK — Matt Pavelich, the first linesman inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame, has died. He was 92. Pavelich officiated games in 19 consecutive Stanley Cup Finals from 1961-79 as part of his 23 seasons working in the NHL. He took part in 1,727 regular season and 245 playoff games during that stretch before serving as the league's supervisor of officials and going into the Hall in 1987. Commissioner Gary Bettman called Pavelich a true icon of the profession. “No linesman in the history of the National Hockey League was more universally respected nor more widely admired than Matt Pavelich,” Bettman said in a statement. “Pavelich personified professionalism and integrity while possessing a warm personal touch that enabled him to develop working relationships with players and coaches.”

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images The hockey world is still reeling from Friday’s stunning news that superstar winger Nikita Kucherov has requested a trade from the Tampa Bay Lightning . Lightning head coach Jon Cooper, for his part, is doing his best to restore a sense of normalcy for the remainder of the season, at least. Cooper spoke to the media ahead of Tampa Bay’s game against the Nashville Predators on Saturday, addressing Kucherov’s trade request and what it may or may not mean for his team this season. “I will sit here and tell you nothing has changed in what our goals are this year — just, maybe, the context of how it is going to go about,” Cooper said. “Kuch is 100 percent a part of this team. Keeping Kucherov in the fold and his team focused are essential to maintaining the Lightning’s Stanley Cup aspirations. items.summary: Forwards Andre Burakovsky and Warren Foegele are set to miss the next three to four weeks with injuries, head coach Travis Green said before Ottawa’s showdown against the San Jose Sharks on Saturday.
items.body: The Ottawa Senators ' forward depth has taken a hit for the next few weeks. Forwards Andre Burakovsky and Warren Foegele are set to miss the next three to four weeks with injuries, head coach Travis Green said before Ottawa's showdown against the San Jose Sharks on Saturday. Burakovsky suffered a lower-body injury in Friday's game against the Los Angeles Kings. It's unclear how he got hurt, but he logged 4:54 of ice time before being ruled out midway through the second period. The 13-year NHL vet is in his first season with the Senators and has made eight appearances without recording a point. Burakovsky owns a minus-two rating through 88:03 of ice time, with four blocks and three hits in that span. Foegele, meanwhile, was placed on the injured list Friday with a knee injury. He was hurt in Tuesday's game against the Vegas Golden Knights after a knee-on-knee collision with Jeremy Lauzon in the third period. The 30-year-old has had a steady start to his first full season with the Senators after being acquired from the Los Angeles Kings at last year's trade deadline. He has one goal and three assists in 13 games, averaging 12:04 of ice time per night.

items.summary: The Boston Bruins unexpectedly opened the season with one of the NHL's best records. That kind of success won't last, but it's all about banking points
items.body: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images The Boston Bruins Aren't As Good As Their Record Indicates, But It Doesn't Matter Ryan Lambert Partner Oct 31, 2026 6:00 PM Published Oct 31, 2026 6:00 PM The Boston Bruins unexpectedly opened the season with one of the NHL's best records. That kind of success won't last, but it's all about banking points Few people would have projected that the Boston Bruins would be the top team in the Atlantic as October drew to a close. Yet they're sitting on 19 points in 14 games, with the NHL's second-best goal differential at plus-18. How are they doing it? items.body: Register Login Maple Leafs Activate Chris Tanev Off IR By Brian La Rose | at October 31, 2026 12:57 pm The Maple Leafs will welcome back a key veteran defenseman tonight against Vancouver. Chris Tanev has been activated off injured reserve, according to the NHL’s media site, meaning he will be back to take on one of his former teams. Tanev sustained a lower-body injury three weeks ago in Colorado in his sixth game of the season, receiving a week-to-week designation soon after. At the time, the thought was that his designation could last for up to six weeks but he’ll be back in half that time. The 36-year-old is a key shutdown defender for Toronto when he’s in the lineup. The problem is that the oft-injured veteran has been hurt more than he has played over the last two seasons. Tanev was limited to just 11 appearances last season with an injury that required late clearance heading into training camp this year. He’s now missed nine of 15 games in the early going this season. The Maple Leafs enter play tonight as the highest-scoring team in the NHL but sit outside a playoff spot thanks to being in the bottom five league-wide defensively in terms of goals allowed. Tanev should definitely help on the defensive side of things and should also help augment a penalty kill that sits second in the league heading into play today with a 92.3% success rate. Toronto had an active roster spot so no corresponding move needed to be made to bring Tanev onto the roster. He will likely take the place of Dakota Mermis in the lineup, who logged less than 10 minutes in Thursday’s loss against Seattle.

items.title: Opinion: Unlike Hellebuyck And Larkin, Nikita Kucherov Is Doing The Lightning A Solid
items.summary: Nikita Kucherov shocked the NHL by requesting a trade from the Tampa Bay Lightning, but unlike Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin, he is doing his team a solid by doing so.
items.body: James Guillory-Imagn Images James Guillory-Imagn Images Opinion: Unlike Hellebuyck And Larkin, Nikita Kucherov Is Doing The Lightning A Solid Ken Campbell Partner Oct 31, 2026 4:54 PM Published Oct 31, 2026 4:54 PM Nikita Kucherov shocked the NHL by requesting a trade from the Tampa Bay Lightning, but unlike Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin, he is doing his team a solid by doing so. Wow, this one is seismic. Among the superstars in the NHL who are asking/demanding they be moved, there's probably not a person in hockey who had Tampa Bay Lightning star Nikita Kucherov on their bingo card. With 13-plus seasons, two Hart Trophies, two Art Ross Trophies, two Stanley Cups, and more than 1,100 career points as the franchise’s leading scorer, Kucherov looked like as sure a bet as you could find to finish his career with the team that drafted him. More Videos But, unlike Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin, Kucherov is actually doing his team a favor with his public declaration. For so many reasons, this is different than the other two. And when the dust settles and emotions subside, the Lightning are going to be happy Kucherov greased his own skids out of town.

Along with Captain America Hilary Knight coming into her record 16th WWC appearance, the U.S. has extensive winning pedigree. Veterans such as Alex Carpenter, Megan Keller and Jesse Compher are all looking to add another medal to their trophy case, while youngsters such as Laila Edwards, Abbey Murphy and Olympic MVP Caroline Harvey look to further solidify themselves as superstars. Aerin Frankel and Gwyneth Philips backstopped the team to the gold at the 2025 WWC and Olympics this past February, with the duo making history in Milan. items.summary: Chris Cuthbert grew up listening to Foster Hewitt and never imagined he would one day be receiving the Hockey Hall of Fame media award named after the legendary Canadian broadcaster.
items.body: Broadcasting icon's legendary calls include 'Golden Goal' for Canada at 2010 Olympics Chris Cuthbert grew up listening to Foster Hewitt and never imagined he would one day be receiving the Hockey Hall of Fame media award named after the legendary Canadian broadcaster. Cuthbert, this year's recipient of the Foster Hewitt Memorial Award for his outstanding contribution to broadcasting, will be honored at the Hockey Hall of Fame media luncheon in Toronto on Nov. 9. "It's overwhelming and it's the ultimate honor for an NHL broadcaster for sure," the 69-year-old told NHL.com. "I may be one of the last of the recipients who grew up listening to Foster Hewitt. He was the first guy to set the dream in motion. I'd go to bed at night with Foster Hewitt on the radio under the pillow listening to him." Cuthbert has become a Canadian broadcasting icon in his own right as the play-by-play voice for a generation of hockey fans. His call of Sidney Crosby 's overtime winner against the United States at the 2010 Vancouver Olympics has been compared to that of Hewitt's in Game 8 of the 1972 Summit Series when Paul Henderson scored the winning goal for Canada against the Soviet Union. Cuthbert was 15 when Hewitt famously exclaimed, "Here's a shot, Henderson made a wild stab for it and fell. Here's another shot, right in front, they score! Henderson has scored for Canada!" More than 37 years later, Cuthbert had a famous line of his own: "Crosby scores! Sidney Crosby, the golden goal and Canada has a once-in-a-lifetime Olympic gold!" Like Hewitt's famous call, Canadian hockey fans remember where they were listening to Cuthbert in the gold medal final. items.title: Reeling Jets fall to Panthers for eighth straight loss
items.body: SUNRISE, Fla. — Anton Lundell had a hat trick, Seth Jones capped a record-setting month with a goal and two assists, and the Florida Panthers topped the reeling Winnipeg Jets 5-2 on Friday night for their sixth win in eight games. Jones finished October with 18 points — two goals and 16 assists — to break the record for most points by a Florida defenseman in any month. Keith Yandle had 17 points for the Panthers in March 2018. Kyle Connor had his team-best 11th goal for Winnipeg, which dropped both ends of a home-and-home with Florida this week and is winless in its last eight games — going 0-6-2 in that span. Morgan Barron had his first goal of the season midway through the third to get the Jets to 3-2, but Lundell's second of the night restored Florida's two-goal edge. Lundell finished off the hat trick — Florida's fifth already this season — with an empty-netter with 1:39 left. Akira Schmid stopped 22 shots for Florida, which remains without standout forwards Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand because of injuries. Both resumed skating this week; Marchand could be back in about three weeks and Barkov in about four, Panthers coach Paul Maurice said. Florida's Bokondji Imama and Winnipeg's Tyrel Bauer brawled just 2:04 into the game, a reenactment of sorts of their still-talked-about fight in the AHL in 2024. They went at it for more than a minute Friday and — similar to what happened at the end of their fight two years ago — shared a respectful nod toward the other when it was over. The Panthers entered Friday having played only three home games this season, the fewest in the NHL. More than half the league had logged at least seven home games going into the day.

items.summary: Connor Hellebuyck stopped 19 shots, Arseny Gritsyuk and Jack Hughes each scored twice and the New Jersey Devils beat the Vegas Golden Knights 5-2 on Friday.
items.body: LAS VEGAS — Connor Hellebuyck stopped 19 shots, Arseny Gritsyuk and Jack Hughes each scored twice and the New Jersey Devils beat the Vegas Golden Knights 5-2 on Friday. Hellebuyck, who spent his first 11 seasons in the NHL with the Winnipeg Jets, had his second win since the Devils acquired him Oct. 23 . The three-time Vezina Trophy also was in goal Tuesday night in Dallas in a 5-1 win. Gritsyuk has scored at least a goal in six of the last eight games and has 10 points during the stretch. Luke Hughes also scored for New Jersey. The Devils improved to 10-1-0 when the Hughes brothers score in the same game. Mark Stone and Ivan Barbashev scored for the Golden Knights, and Adin Hill stopped 26 shots. Luke Hughes got things going early in the first when he rifled a one-timer from the top of the left circle past Hill. Stone tied it when he deflected Mitch Marner’s blast from the point past Hellebuyck. Barbashev gave the Knights a 2-1 lead moments later when he tapped Marner’s pass home after a picture-perfect cross-crease pass. The lead didn’t last one minute, as Gritsyuk took advantage of a turnover and sniped Hill top shelf from the left circle. Jack Hughes put New Jersey back in front when he stole the puck from Jack Eichel in the neutral zone, then passed it to himself through Stone’s legs before beating Hill. Gritsyuk scored his second goal by backhanding his rebound after Hill blocked his first attempt.

items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” After a thorough examination of all available replays, there was no conclusive evidence that the puck shot by Florida’s Dmitry Kulikov at 12:03 (7:57 elapsed time) was deflected before going out of play . Therefore, the call on the ice stands. The decision was made in accordance with Rule 38.2 (d) which states, in part, that a team may request a Coach’s Challenge “When a minor penalty for delaying the game has been assessed under Rule 63.2 (iii) for shooting or batting the puck out of play from the defending zone. This will only apply to delay of game penalties when the shot/batted puck is determined to have subsequently deflected off a player, stick, glass or boards, etc., and not a judgment call.” Therefore, an additional minor penalty was assessed to Florida (in addition to the existing delay of game penalty).

items.body: Hayden Hodgson will be watching the next two games from the press box. The Ottawa Senators forward has been suspended for two games for boarding, the NHL's Department of Player Safety announced Friday. The punishment comes after Hodgson received a game misconduct and major penalty for boarding Los Angeles Kings defenceman Brandt Clarke on Thursday night. Hodgson took a run at Clarke, charging in at 21 m.p.h., according to the game broadcast. Clarke was just below the goal line when he was driven into the boards. The hit caused a brief scrum, and the Kings' Erik Haula received a two-minute penalty for roughing Hodgson. Clarke was ruled out for the rest of the game for what the Kings called an upper-body injury. The play with 8:45 left in the second period came shortly after the Kings scored three goals in 4:03 to take a 4-1 lead and chase goalie Jonas Johansson. Hodgson has played in only 24 NHL games over five seasons, but including Thursday, has amassed 51 minutes in penalties. Hodgson was fined $2,018, the maximum allowed under the terms of the collective bargaining agreement, in October 2025 for boarding Montreal's Alex Newhook in a pre-season game. He has a long history of suspensions — 20 games worth — in the American Hockey League for elbowing and other offences over the past five seasons. He’ll forfeit $8,763 in salary as a result of the suspension. He'll miss games Saturday at San Jose and Sunday at Anaheim. He's eligible to return Wednesday at Buffalo. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources As the hockey world gets set for Russia’s return to international hockey, some people aren’t quite ready yet. In the wake of the Court of Arbitration for Sport announcing that the Russian Ice Hockey Federation will be permitted to submit teams for international ice hockey tournament , other international sporting federations have released statements against the ruling, most notably Hockey Canada. items.body: Register Login Ducks Assign Nikita Klepov To OHL By Brennan McClain | at October 30, 2026 3:32 pm According to a team announcement , the Anaheim Ducks have returned forward Nikita Klepov to the OHL’s Saginaw Spirit. Klepov will remain with the Spirit through the end of the 2026-27 campaign and attempt to crack Anaheim’s roster next season. Because he didn’t reach the 10-game mark, or even come close, the Ducks can now slide Klepov’s entry-level contract despite him making his NHL debut. Klepov finishes his first four NHL contests going scoreless with a -2 rating, averaging 13:03 of ice time per game. On the one hand, it’s a smart move by Anaheim; even though Klepov had five more games of eligibility, the recent 15th overall pick should get more playing time. Now, Klepov can pick up where he left off with Saginaw. He scored 37 goals and 97 points in 67 games for the Spirit last season. Unfortunately for Saginaw, the Kitchener Rangers swept them in the 2026 OHL Playoffs conference quarterfinals. On the other hand, the Ducks may have missed the mark by signing Klepov to his entry-level contract so early. Before signing his first professional contract, Klepov was committed to play at Michigan State University for the 2026-27 campaign. However, since he signed a professional deal, he was no longer eligible for the NCAA. Instead, Klepov returns to a level he has already dominated after making four NHL appearances. If the Ducks weren’t planning to give him more opportunity, it would have been wiser to have him remain without a contract so he could play for the Spartans.

And like the guy or not, there is a two-word answer for all of it: Mike Babcock. “You're getting called out on whatever you're not doing right to help the team win,” Leon Draisaitl said on Friday. items.title: Six key takeaways from the first month of the NHL season
items.summary: What have we learned through the first month of the NHL season? We take a look around the league at some takeaways as the calendar gets set to flip to November.
items.body: One full month of NHL action is behind us. With more than five months of regular-season play still ahead of us, there is still so much that can happen. What we think we may know about the season less than 20 per cent of the way in could change drastically by April — or, some early signs could stick and become season-long narratives. At this one-month touchpoint, we take a look around the league at some key early takeaways: At least three teams from the Atlantic — and maybe four! — will finish with crushing disappointment We knew this would be a competitive division, but this start has been wild. Everybody in the Atlantic has a points percentage over .500 — Toronto currently ranks last with a .533 points percentage and the Maple Leafs have felt competitive with a 7-6-2 record. Only two teams — Detroit (minus-1) and Buffalo (minus-7) — have a negative goal differential. All of these teams have playoff expectations — even Detroit, with all the drama around Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson, has a 10-year playoff drought it is trying to squash this season. We already see that at least three teams will head into the summer with some very difficult questions about firings and roster changes to answer — only because of the division they're in. Now, 14 games at a point-per-game pace doesn’t automatically make Pettersson a Hart Trophy contender or even a top 25 scorer in the NHL. But if he can return to a 70+ point pace, he and his contract could have value in the new NHL economy, where some players are getting deals north of $20MM annually. If it seems crazy, that’s because it is. This past summer rewrote the NHL salary landscape, and it appears player salaries could keep trending upward. Sabres’ forward Tage Thompson led the way with a five-point night , fueled by a natural hat trick and two assists. Buffalo’s top line of Thompson, Zach Benson and Peyton Krebs dominated in possession and expected goals , as well as on the scoresheet, as Benson recorded a goal and two assists while Krebs had three assists. On Friday’s episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Tyler Yaremchuk and former NHL goaltender Carter Hutton discuss the Sabres’ win and how impressive Buffalo’s three forwards were. Tyler Yaremchuk : That Sabres’ top line was absolute dynamite in this victory, combining for 11 points in the win. It was a good win for Buffalo, who so far have lost most games than they’ve won, but they’re trying to get hot, and last night was a good step in that direction. Carter Hutton : It was a good step, especially with the Toronto Maple Leafs dropping a few games. You’re trying to get points in the Atlantic Division and keep pace. I think for Peyton Krabs, being in a situation where he’s goalless with seven assists, but he’s learning how to play with a player like Tage Thompson. Thompson is one of those guys where you don’t need to be the elite finisher, because you already have that guy. You can just find a way to settle in to the offensive zone, win pucks, win your battles, generate space, because Tage has the art of finding soft areas on the ice. If you can facilitate that, you can make a lot of money and play a long time playing beside a guy like that. We’ve seen numerous times where Batman needs his Robin, and that’s a good role to be in. items.summary: In the latest 32 Thoughts, Elliotte Friedman writes about what could happen next with Dylan Larkin now that he’s stepped away from the Red Wings, plus much more.
items.body: • As Larkin walks away from Red Wings, where does that leave Simon Edvinsson ? • Minnesota's tricky situation with Quinn Hughes • The most fitting endorsement ever The Dylan Larkin Detroit Divorce became official Thursday, with the team’s former captain informing the club he would no longer play for them; the Red Wings responded by suspending him without pay and removing his nameplate from the team’s dressing room. Of all the players who, last summer, asked for trades or said they wouldn’t be re-signing once current contracts expired, several sources said Larkin had the toughest time handling the blowback. While others blocked it out, got their wish or stayed away, he threw himself into the fire, hoping playing for the winged wheel until a trade occurred would calm the storm. And, I was told on several occasions that he was concerned how commentary about his situation would be received by his teammates. That said, less than one week after Connor Hellebuyck was sent east, Larkin’s agent, Pat Brisson, met face-to-face with his client and announced the player “had enough.” He’s not the only one. Please God, use your omnipotent power to get Bill Guerin or Kent Hughes (or anyone else) to make the trade so we can all stop talking about it. One of my working theories is that Brisson/Larkin are aware of an offer they deem acceptable, even if that feeling is not shared by interim GM Shawn Horcoff. Anyone who covers the NHL will tell you things change with one phone call. But, as this situation went supernova, there was nothing close. But it’s not entirely likely that Robertson, who inked a one-year, $12MM contract to remain with the Stars for the 2026-27 season, will ink a deal right away. According to Pierre LeBrun of The Athletic , he guesses that Robertson’s camp might wait until other player contracts are settled with teams so they can evaluate the current state of the market for him. It was expected by many that the situation of Robertson would be a major storyline over the summer. The Seattle Kraken had nearly landed the player, having made a deal with Dallas that would include an eight-year extension for $125MM, which would make him one of the league’s highest-paid players. However, Robertson settled with the Stars and both sides ultimately ‘kicked the tires’ for when he will officially become a UFA entering his 28-year-old season, which is surely to be the peak of his prime. It’s already hard to consider how much the market will change when looking at what transpired this past offseason to get ahead of it. Leo Carlsson received a lucrative offer sheet of five years for $18MM a season from the Philadelphia Flyers, which the Anaheim Ducks matched. items.summary: It’s a scary time of year in the NHL as teams begin to realize things may not be going according to plan. Sportsnet’s Michael Amato breaks down four lingering problems across the league.
items.body: It’s a scary time of year. Haunted houses and horror movies abound, but perhaps most terrifying is the sight of kids full of sugar after a night of trick-or-treating. There are reasons for some NHL squads to be scared, too. Every off-season plan looks perfect in September, but come Halloween, you start to realize things aren’t going exactly as planned. Inevitable injuries, lines not clicking the way teams envisioned or holes in the roster not able to be filled are all issues different general mangers are trying to solve for around the league. It’s getting close to the time where teams may have to take action in order to improve their situation where they can. Let’s look at four teams and why they have a reason to be scared right now. We’re just a couple of days away from November and Quinn Hughes is still without a contract extension. Maybe there’s no reason to panic and he and Bill Guerin will work something out, but every day that goes by without an extension brings Hughes that much closer to free agency. It sounds like the Wild are willing to give Hughes a max deal for whatever term he wishes, so you’d think the ball is in his court at this point. In other words, if he wanted to extend in Minnesota, wouldn’t he have done so by now? We also know that playing with his brothers is very important to Hughes and both Jack and Luke currently play for the New Jersey Devils. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images The Dylan Larkin situation is coming to a head, as the former Detroit Red Wings captain will officially no longer play for his hometown team. Between public statements from his agent, Pat Brisson, and team interim GM Shawn Horcoff, news broke on Thursday that the 30-year-old center would sit out until his trade request was met. Larkin’s ask has been a tricky situation, as the player possesses a full no-movement clause and has been very specific with his preferred list of teams. Even with an expanded list, Larkin has ruled out all Canadian clubs, which has left Horcoff in a tough spot trying to get back fair value for the 2014-first-round pick. One club that has been consistently tied to Larkin is the Minnesota Wild , who have all of their chips in the middle with the Quinn Hughes situation looming large. General manager Bill Guerin knows Larkin well from international play with Team USA, and according to TSN’s Pierre LeBrun on Thursday, the Wild have been the most active team in trying to acquire Larkin’s services. Speaking with Wild sources over the last number of days, Daily Faceoff was told that the Red Wings are being “unrealistic” in what they are looking for in return for Larkin. It has long been speculated that the Wild have been dangling center Danila Yurov as the centerpiece of a trade; clearly that hasn’t moved the needle enough for the Red Wings . Sokolowski-USA TODAY Sports IIHF 'Expresses Its Disappointment' In Decision To Allow Russia To Play In International Tournaments Michael Traikos Partner Oct 30, 2026 1:09 PM Published Oct 30, 2026 1:09 PM The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Russia will be allowed to return to international hockey for 2027. And the International Ice Hockey Federation is not happy. On Friday, the IIHF released a statement saying it "expresses its disappointment with the decision." Russia has been banned from international events since 2022 , as a result of its invasion of Ukraine. But in July, the International Olympic Committe lifted the suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee, paving the way for Russia to return to international competition. According to the sports court ruling, there was a lack of sufficient evidence to support the IIHF's security concerns on keeping Russia out of international competitions. However, in its statement on Friday, the IIHF said it "disagrees … with the ruling and maintains that its decisions were necessary to protect the safety and security of all participants and safeguard the integrity of its competitions." In a social media post on Telegram , Russian Sports Minister Mikhail Degtyaryov wrote that CAS "recognized the demands of the Russian Hockey Federation on key points as justified." Despite its concerns, the IIHF announced that it will act in accordance with the CAS's ruling, which could immediately impact the international calendar. The first event effected by the CAS's ruling is the IIHF World Junior Championship 2027 in Edmonton and Red Deer, Alta., which begins later this year. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Nick Turchiaro-USA TODAY Sports A massive ruling in the world of international hockey. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Ottawa Senators forward Hayden Hodgson was assessed a five-minute major penalty and a game misconduct for boarding Los Angeles Kings defenseman Brandt Clarke during Thursday’s game at Crypto.com Arena. Hodgson, 30, sent Clarke flying into the boards with a hard, forceful check from behind at the 11:15 mark of the second period on Thursday. Clarke was slow to get to his feet after the hit but remained in the game, while the other Kings players on the ice immediately took exception. Kings forward Erik Haula was assessed a two-minute roughing penalty for his role in the ensuing melee, but the Kings still ended up with a power play, on which Artemi Panarin scored his eighth goal of the 2026-27 season to put the home side up by a 5-1 score. An undrafted 6’2″ winger from Windsor, Ont., Hodgson has spent the majority of his professional career to date in the AHL and ECHL. Thursday’s game was the 24th of his NHL career, and his 17th with the Senators. items.title: Seider reacts to Larkin leaving Red Wings: ‘Turn the page’
items.summary: Moritz Seider is looking ahead as his former captain waits at home for a trade.
items.body: Moritz Seider is looking ahead as his former captain waits at home for a trade. The Detroit Red Wings ' top defenceman said, "It's good to put it in the past and turn the page," after Dylan Larkin left the team and was suspended without pay on Thursday. "Whoever we get, whatever pick we get, we'll have players that are happy to be here," Seider said after the Red Wings beat the Chicago Blackhawks 4-1. "We just have to make sure we get them ready to be part of our team." Larkin requested a trade out of Detroit in the spring but had been playing while awaiting a deal, even scoring a big goal late in a win over the Oilers on Monday. But on Thursday, interim general manager Shawn Horcoff announced that Larkin "has informed us that he will no longer play for the Detroit Red Wings," so the team suspended the veteran centre as they weigh offers. The news came hours before the Red Wings hosted former teammate Patrick Kane and the rival Chicago Blackhawks in a game broadcast on ESPN, but after a slow start, Detroit rallied to win thanks to a hat trick from newcomer Viktor Arvidsson to improve to 6-4-3 on the season. "Obviously it meant a little more," Seider said of winning after the drama of the day. "I think it came down to this is our squad and we have a really good group in here." Seider, who is likely to succeed Larkin as captain, said he wishes nothing but the best to his now-former teammate. "Obviously it's tough but in the end you want him to be happy and if that's not here hopefully it's somewhere else," Seider said. "It's kinda hard to put that player aspect aside and just see it as a friend, but ultimately that's my goal... Nevertheless, we still have a hell of a group in here."

Cooley became the third Pittsburgh native with a hat trick against the Penguins, joining Brandon Saad and R.J. Umberger. He had two first-period goals to give the Mammoth an early 2-0 lead, and scored in the third for his third career hat trick. In overtime, Sergachev beat Arturs Silovs off a rebound in front. Sebastian Cossa stopped 31 shots for the Mammoth, who have won three of their last five games overall. Utah is 5-0-0 after a loss and 8-0-0 when leading after two periods. Rickard Rakell had a short-handed goal, and Erik Karlsson also scored for Pittsburgh. Silovs made 30 saves.

items.title: Islanders’ Ryan Pulock leaves game with upper-body injury
items.summary: Pulock played just two shifts in the game before exiting after an awkward board battle with Yakov Trenin.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images The New York Islanders announced that defenseman Ryan Pulock will not return to Thursday’s game against the Minnesota Wild due to an upper-body injury. Pulock sustained the injury early in the first period of the game, only playing in two shifts before he exited the match. It’s unclear what exactly caused the injury, but the most likely incident was when he was battling along the boards with Yakov Trenin, as he skated gingerly after the fact. He went to the dressing room after and did not return, with the team confirming his absence at the start of the second period. Pulock played just 51 seconds of ice time in those two shifts, with only a hit taken on his stat line before exiting the game. The Islanders were already down 1-0 at the time of his early departure. There’s currently no other updates on Pulock, including the severity of the injury and how much time he’s expected to miss. Islanders head coach Pete DeBoer might give an update after the game, but since the Isles are at the end of a three-game road trip before returning home, it’s likely that a more specific update isn’t provided until a practice or morning skate on Long Island. One big concern from Pulock’s injury is that he had shoulder surgery in the offseason, so an upper-body injury could mean that he re-injured the shoulder. However, the Islanders have not confirmed that is the case. Pulock was off to slow start to the season, as he had just one assist in 13 games before the injury. items.title: Jets rally but fall to Lightning for seventh straight loss
items.body: TAMPA, Fla. — Pontus Holmberg set a career high with four points on a goal and three assists, Brandon Hagel and Anthony Cirelli each had a goal and two assists, and the Tampa Bay Lightning remain unbeaten at home with a 6-4 victory over the Winnipeg Jets on Thursday night. Brayden Point, John Carlson and Conor Geekie all scored for Tampa Bay. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 17 shots. The Lightning improved to 6-0 at home to tie a franchise record to start a season. Neil Pionk, playing his 600th game, scored twice. Kyle Connor and Dylan Samberg also scored for the Jets and Mark Scheifele had three assists. Stuart Skinner allowed five goals on 21 shots before being replaced by Nico Daws to start the third period. Daws finished with nine saves in his Winnipeg debut. Winnipeg is winless (0-5-2) in the past seven games, including three consecutive regulation losses since trading goaltender Connor Hellebuyck to New Jersey. After Point and Pionk traded goals in the first period, Tampa Bay pulled away in the second period with four goals, including three in the final 4:04. Geekie backhanded in a pass from Dominic James at 9:43 before Cirelli scored a power-play goal at 15:56, getting his stick on a cross-crease pass from Holmberg. Carlson made it 4-1 at 18:07 as he one-timed Holmberg's pass from the left faceoff dot. Hagel finished off the period with a tap-in from Cirelli at the back post with 56 seconds left in the period. Winnipeg scored two goals less than two minutes apart in the third to cut into the lead. Perfetti fed Samberg for a one-handed redirect at 7:00 while Pionk scored his second at 8:50, with Dawson Mercer registering his first point with the Jets on the play. Connor scored with 2:49 left to make it a one-goal game.
